title.narrative: Second Panama Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan with a CAT DDO

description.narrative: The PDO is to enhance the Government of Panama's technical and institutional capacity to manage the disaster risk resulting from the occurrence of natural and health-related hazards, including the adverse effects of climate change and disease outbreaks.

The development objectives of the Second Panama Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan in Panama enhance the Government of Panama's technical and institutional capacity to manage the disaster risk resulting from the occurrence of natural and health-related hazards, including the adverse effects of climate change and disease outbreaks. The Government of Panama has adopted the Strategic Framework for the Financial Management of Disaster Risk (2014) to identify, manage and prevent fiscal risk in the event of disasters related to the impact of natural hazards or economic shocks, thus enabling the identification of Theme Areas to reduce the risks of said disasters or hazards. This Strategic Framework focuses on five Strategic Pillars: (i) identification, quantification, and understanding of fiscal risk due to disasters; (ii) incorporation of disaster risk analysis in the planning of public investment; (iii) formulation of components for developing and implementing risk retention and transfer instruments; (iv) development of the domestic insurance market; and (v) strengthening of the State Directorate of Investment, Concessions, and Risks, so it can fulfill its role in designing and implementing financial protection strategies. The National Government is committed to three (3) Policy Areas, including the following Priority Actions associated with disaster risk and climate change. Policy Area 1, strengthening the institutional framework for management and response to the impact of climate and disaster risk in a post-COVID context; Policy Area 2, strengthening climate risk hazards identification and disaster risk assessment capabilities and Policy Area 3, development of territorial responsibilities for disaster risk management.

title.narrative: National-level simulation exercises to test multi-hazard response protocols carried out with satisfaction levels at or above 80 percent according to PAHO best practices

comment.narrative: The indicator is fully met with three simulations conducted. During COP10-MOP3 by WHO FCTC, a fourth simulation addressed multiple threats, including storms, earthquakes, and mass food poisoning. It included air and sea transfers, police coordination, and accessibility for people with reduced mobility through ramps and special ambulances. This simulation is included in the result indicator, totaling four simulations conducted.

title.narrative: Number of multisectoral programs endorsed by the DRM Cabinet

comment.narrative: The indicator is fully met. SINAPROC highlighted the importance of the Gabinete GIRD as a fundamental element for driving multisectoral reforms in risk management at both policy and institutional levels. This is noted as a regional example, particularly due to its executive role in analyzing and approving initiatives and the significance of dialogue between political and technical levels. The national DRM policy, national DRM implementation plan, recovery framework, and response plan have been approved and are under implementation.

title.narrative: Percentage of SINAPROC's staff certified as risk managers nationwide as per the new Civil Protection Career provisions

comment.narrative: The indicator is fully met. A virtual asynchronous course on Comprehensive Disaster Risk Management (CDRM) was delivered nationally, with 154 SINAPROC staff participating (70.6% of 218 invited), exceeding the 35% target. Knowledge was assessed through test-based forms. Participants included 59 women (38.31%) and 95 men (61.69%).

title.narrative: Number of economic activities and sectors informed through seasonal forecasts emitted by the NMHS

comment.narrative: The indicator is met through the providing of forecasts to the power, agricultural (via agro-climatic tables), and health sectors (for drought and potable water planning). In Chiriqui, IMHPA collaborates with IDAAN (Water company) with monthly rainfall forecasts and with MINSA on disease prevention like Chikungunya. Support is also given to the marine authority on a fishermen's bulletin and with the Ministry of Culture on rain quality monitoring in historical areas like Casco Viejo.

title.narrative: Percentage of female members within the Civil Protection General Directorate

comment.narrative: SINAPROC confirms that women make up 37% of the staff in the General Directorate of Civil Protection, still below the established target of 50%, including both permanent and volunteer personnel. The current review of the indicator shows a variation from the 41% reported during the 2023 supervision mission. This change reflects recent shifts in the organizational structure resulting from the government transition process.

title.narrative: Approval of the NMHss organizational structure, budget, and staffing plan by the Institute's board of directors

comment.narrative: NMHS’s organizational structure, budget, and staffing plan have been approved in December 2022 and the organization advances in the tendering process for the construction of its future headquarters.

title.narrative: Percentage of municipalities with updated Strategic District Plans (PED) or Land Use Plans (POT) integrating Disaster Risk Management (DRM) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA) criteria

comment.narrative: The indicator was updated for the extension of the operation. The new indicator measures the percentage of municipalities with updated Strategic District Plans (PED) or Land Use Plans (POT) integrating Disaster Risk Management (DRM) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA) criteria, with a baseline of 0% in 2025 and a target of 25% by 2028. During a meeting with DDT and MIVIOT, 7 to 8 POTs were identified as potential baseline documents, pending review to confirm the inclusion of DRM and CCA criteria. Both institutions agreed to provide the list of relevant plans and recognized the need to strengthen municipal capacities. It was agreed that MIVIOT and DDT will present a plan and methodology to achieve the target, while DICRE will coordinate efforts. All parties reaffirmed their commitment to collaborate, with World Bank technical support planned for May to define a joint action roadmap.
